subject: Procurement: instrumentation & metrics access for SLOs
messages:
From: Sam Cardona <sam.cardona@finedge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Procurement questionnaire: how Redwood measures latency/uptime

Hi Vanessa,

We're running procurement diligence ahead of our PoC and have a short set of questions about how Redwood measures and publishes uptime/latency SLOs so our security and SRE teams can sign off. Can you confirm the following?

1) Which metrics do you use for availability and latency (examples: successful request rate, P95/P99 tail latency, connection errors)?
2) Measurement window and SLA window (rolling 30d/90d? calendar month?).
3) Monitoring stack (Grafana/Prometheus, sampling rates) and whether customers can get read-only access to the dashboards.
4) Alerting cadence and escalation (who gets paged for infra vs model-quality incidents?).
5) Evidence for historical performance (CSV or dashboard snapshots) and retention period for time-series.
6) Exception path: how do you handle temporary carve-outs for PoC traffic spikes and what rollback criteria do you require?

If possible, please attach any short instrumentation or monitoring summaries. We'd like to close the loop on this by next Wednesday so procurement can finish the contract.

Thanks,
Sam Cardona
Procurement Manager, FinEdge
sam.cardona@finedge.com

---
Note: attaching our internal questionnaire in a follow-up if helpful.
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Cardona <sam.cardona@finedge.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: how Redwood measures latency/uptime

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; attaching a 2-page instrumentation summary and a one-click Grafana invite link. Happy to walk through live (20-30m) if that helps.

1) Metrics we publish:
   - Availability: successful request rate (5xx/4xx normalized), measured per-route and per-model; monthly uptime percentage for routed traffic.
   - Latency: P50/P95/P99 for server processing time (request accept -> last token sent); we also surface token throughput for heavy batching workloads.
   - Errors: connection failures, internal service errors, model runtime exceptions.

2) Measurement windows: default rolling 30-day window for alerts and monthly calendar window for contractual uptime. SLA breaches are evaluated on calendar month unless a custom term is agreed.

3) Monitoring stack & access: Prometheus + Grafana. We can grant read-only org-level access scoped to your account (no cross-customer data). The invite linked in grafana_readonly_invite_link.txt is a short-lived onboarding token for your SREs. Sampling: we retain full 1s-resolution key-series for 30d, downsampled thereafter.

4) Alerting & escalation: Operational infra alerts (node/GPU failures, orchestration) are routed to Redwood on-call (pager) and ops@redwood.com. Customer-facing SLA degradations (sustained latency above threshold) generate an incident ticket and we notify named contacts configured in the MAP. For PoC we typically set an accelerated notification channel to loop in SEs.

5) Evidence & retention: We can provide dashboard snapshots (CSV export) for prior 90 days on request. Time-series retention: raw 30d, downsampled 365d. Audit logs for API calls retained per contract term.

6) Exception path / carve-outs: We support temporary carve-outs for PoC with a short mutual action plan (MAP): a defined timebox, traffic thresholds, and rollback criteria. See the attached summary for a sample MAP template. Proposed default for PoCs: 30-day carve-out with explicit traffic-level gate (e.g., sustained >2x expected baseline) and continuous monitoring; rollback if P99 exceeds agreed threshold for more than three consecutive 1-hour windows.

Attachments: slo_instrumentation_summary.pdf (instrumentation diagram + metric definitions), grafana_readonly_invite_link.txt (one-click invite), retention_policy_snippet.docx (short excerpt).

If you want, we can propose a MAP draft and pricing impact for the carve-out on a short call — I can bring Priyom (SE) to cover monitoring details.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Cardona <sam.cardona@finedge.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Procurement questionnaire: how Redwood measures latency/uptime — proposed MAP and exception wording

Priyom / Karthik — forwarding Sam's thread. They want a contract-ready exception path for a PoC and an anonymized 30-day snapshot. My suggested approach below; please confirm if this is acceptable or propose edits. I copied Sam so they see our working draft.

Proposed MAP / PoC carve-out (draft to include in SOW):
- Timebox: 30 calendar days starting on first production-like traffic spike.
- Scope: applies only to the specific model endpoints and routes listed in the SOW.
- Monitoring gates: Redwood will enable an accelerated alerting policy for the FinEdge account; P95 and P99 will be computed on server processing time.
- Numeric thresholds: Temporary p99 ceiling = 1.5x standard contractual p99 for the model class; if p99 exceeds this ceiling for three consecutive 1-hour windows, Redwood will initiate mitigation steps (auto-scaling and cache warmup).
- Rollback criteria: If, after mitigation, p99 remains above the ceiling for more than 6 hours total within a 24-hour window, either party may pause PoC traffic and revert to the prior routing policy.
- Notification & owners: Redwood on-call (ops@redwood.com) for infra; SE on-call (priyom_das@redwood.com) for monitoring/model quality; FinEdge to provide one recipient for urgent notifications.
- Evidence: Redwood will share a 30-day anonymized CSV export of per-route p95/p99 and success rates before the PoC start date.

Priyom — can you prepare the anonymized 30-day CSV and confirm that the proposed numeric thresholds are realistic for a PoC? Karthik — please confirm there's no policy/legal blocker to the rollback language and the proposed notification matrix.

Thanks — if we can get both thumbs-up I will finalize the MAP and send Sam a clean version they can paste into the SOW.
